problems.quote: ISRO (established 1969 under Department of Space)
problems.problem: ISRO was established in 1969 under the Department of Atomic Energy; the Department of Space was created in 1972.
problems.correction: ISRO (established 1969 under Department of Atomic Energy, later under Department of Space)
problems.verifierReason: ISRO founded 1969 under DAE; DoS created 1972. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: NBRC (National Bioethics Committee)
problems.problem: NBRC stands for National Brain Research Centre; the correct acronym for National Bioethics Committee is NBC.
problems.correction: NBC (National Bioethics Committee)
problems.verifierReason: NBRC is National Brain Research Centre; National Bioethics Committee is NBC.

problems.quote: ICMR-NIB (National Institute of Biomedical Genomics)
problems.problem: National Institute of Biomedical Genomics (NIBMG) is an autonomous institute under DBT, not ICMR.
problems.correction: DBT-NIBMG (National Institute of Biomedical Genomics)
problems.verifierReason: NIBMG is under DBT, not ICMR; acronym is NIBMG not NIB.

problems.quote: Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 39(b) and 39(c))
problems.problem: Article 39 is a single article with clauses (b) and (c), not separate articles.
problems.correction: Directive Principles of State Policy (Article 39(b) and (c))
problems.verifierReason: Original incorrectly pluralizes Article 39; correction uses singular Article 39(b) and (c) accurately.

problems.quote: the Nolan Principles (selflessness, integrity, objectivity, accountability, openness, honesty, leadership) adopted by the Indian civil services
problems.problem: The Nolan Principles are UK standards from 1995; they have influenced Indian ethics reforms but have not been formally adopted by the Indian civil services.
problems.correction: the Nolan Principles ... referenced in Indian civil service ethics but not formally adopted
problems.verifierReason: Nolan Principles are UK-origin, not formally adopted by Indian civil services; correction accurate.

problems.quote: procedural fairness mandate of the 73rd Amendment
problems.problem: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment relates to Panchayati Raj institutions, not procedural fairness; procedural fairness derives from Articles 14 and 21.
problems.correction: procedural fairness mandate of Articles 14 and 21
problems.verifierReason: 73rd Amendment concerns Panchayats; procedural fairness stems from Arts 14,21.

problems.quote: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) which recognised the right to disclose in public interest subject to proportionality
problems.problem: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) primarily concerns passive euthanasia/Whistleblower Act implementation; it does not recognise a right to disclose to media subject to proportionality.
problems.correction: the Supreme Court’s judgment in Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) directing operationalisation of the Whistle Blowers Protection Act
problems.verifierReason: 2018 Common Cause judgment directed operationalisation of Whistle Blowers Act, not media disclosure right.

problems.quote: The Personal Data Protection Bill (pending enactment) will codify these safeguards.
problems.problem: The bill has been enacted as the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023; it is no longer pending.
problems.correction: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 codifies these safeguards.
problems.verifierReason: The Personal Data Protection Bill became the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (assented Aug 11, 2023); it is no longer pending.

problems.quote: The emerging 'Algorithmic Accountability Framework' adopted by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) in 2023
problems.problem: MeitY has not adopted an Algorithmic Accountability Framework in 2023; this appears to be an invented policy.
problems.correction: No Algorithmic Accountability Framework has been adopted by MeitY as of 2023.
problems.verifierReason: MeitY did not adopt any 'Algorithmic Accountability Framework' in 2023; the correction accurately reflects its non-existence.

problems.quote: ~25% world
problems.problem: India's thorium reserves (~846,000 tonnes) are ~70% of world reserves (USGS 2023: 1.2 Mt), not 25%; the 25% figure refers to thorium *resources* (IAEA: India 1.07 Mt of 6.4 Mt world).
problems.correction: ~70% of world reserves (USGS)
problems.verifierReason: Original 25% figure misrepresents reserves; correction to ~70% of world reserves is accurate.

problems.quote: fuel safeguarded reactors (Kudankulam, Tarapur, Rawatbhata, Kakrapar, upcoming Kudankulam 3-6)
problems.problem: Kudankulam VVERs use Russian (TVEL) fuel, not Kazakh/Canadian/Australian imports; Kakrapar PHWRs use domestic uranium. Imports fuel Tarapur BWRs and some safeguarded PHWRs (e.g., Rawatbhata 2-6).
problems.correction: fuel safeguarded reactors (Tarapur, Rawatbhata 2-6, and future PHWRs)
problems.verifierReason: Original list incorrectly includes Kudankulam and Kakrapar; correction listing Tarapur, Rawatbhata 2‑6 and future PHWRs is correct.

problems.quote: moral motivation, moral character, and situational pressures (Rest's four‑component model) mediate the translation of reasoning into action
problems.problem: Rest's four-component model comprises moral sensitivity, moral judgment, moral motivation, and moral character; situational pressures are not a component but an external moderator.
problems.correction: Rest's four‑component model (moral sensitivity, judgment, motivation, character) mediates translation of reasoning into action; situational pressures are external moderators.
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates model components and includes situational pressures as a component; correction accurately lists four components and classifies situational pressures as external moderators.

problems.quote: Section 12 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 (as adapted for local bodies by the respective state legislation)
problems.problem: Section 12 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 deals with appointment of the Lokpal Chairperson and Members, not creation of Ethics Officers in municipal corporations.
problems.correction: under the respective state legislation on local bodies
problems.verifierReason: Section 12 concerns Lokpal appointments; Ethics Officers derive from state local body laws.

problems.quote: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1996) by recognising the “public trust” doctrine
problems.problem: The public trust doctrine was recognised by the Supreme Court in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997), not in a 1996 M.C. Mehta v. Union of India case.
problems.correction: M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997) by recognising the “public trust” doctrine
problems.verifierReason: Public trust doctrine first recognized in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997), not 1996 case.

problems.quote: representation quotas for women, SC/ST, and persons with disabilities (as mandated by Article 243D and 243T)
problems.problem: Articles 243D and 243T mandate reservation for SC/ST and women (not less than one-third); they do not provide quotas for persons with disabilities.
problems.correction: representation quotas for women and SC/ST (as mandated by Article 243D and 243T)
problems.verifierReason: Articles 243D/243T mandate SC/ST and women quotas only; no PwD quota.

problems.quote: Section 24 of the General Clauses Act, 1897
problems.problem: Section 24 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 deals with the effect of repeal of enactments; it does not mandate a “reasoned order” format.
problems.correction: the principles of natural justice and administrative law
problems.verifierReason: Section 24 GCA deals with repeal effect; reasoned orders stem from natural justice.

problems.quote: Rule 173 of the GFR mandates that all procurements above the prescribed threshold be conducted through the Government e‑Marketplace (GeM)
problems.problem: Rule 173 of GFR 2017 mandates procurement through GeM for all goods/services available on GeM, not only above a monetary threshold.
problems.correction: Rule 173 of the GFR mandates that all procurements of goods and services available on GeM be conducted through the Government e‑Marketplace (GeM)
problems.verifierReason: Rule 173 GFR mandates GeM for all available goods/services, not threshold-based.

problems.quote: post‑1975 emergency reforms
problems.problem: The Emergency (1975‑77) was a period of authoritarian rule, not strong vigilance reforms; the phrase is historically inaccurate and likely confuses post‑Emergency reforms (after 1977) or the 1964 establishment of the Central Vigilance Commission.
problems.correction: post‑Emergency reforms
problems.verifierReason: Original phrase mislabels reforms; correct term is post‑Emergency reforms.

problems.quote: State of Karnataka v. Union of India (1977), the Supreme Court held that the Centre cannot encroach on State legislative competence under the guise of executive action, affirming constitutional morali
problems.problem: The term "constitutional morality" was not used in the 1977 judgment; it is a later judicial concept (prominent post-2018). The case affirmed federal distribution of powers, not constitutional morality.
problems.correction: State of Karnataka v. Union of India (1977), the Supreme Court held that the Centre cannot encroach on State legislative competence under the guise of executive action, affirming federalism as a const
problems.verifierReason: 1977 judgment did not use 'constitutional morality'; it affirmed federalism.

problems.quote: The questionnaire’s 26-item short form reduces respondent burden while retaining reliability
problems.problem: The Ethical Climate Questionnaire (ECQ) originally has 26 items; that is the standard form, not a short form. A short form would be shorter (e.g., 17 items).
problems.correction: The questionnaire’s 26-item standard form reduces respondent burden while retaining reliability
problems.verifierReason: ECQ's 26-item version is the standard form, not a short form; correction fixes terminology.

problems.quote: MeitY “Responsible AI” framework (2024)
problems.problem: MeitY did not publish a "Responsible AI" framework in 2024; the framework is from NITI Aayog (2021).
problems.correction: NITI Aayog’s “Responsible AI” framework (2021)
problems.verifierReason: NITI Aayog published Responsible AI framework in 2021; MeitY did not publish one in 2024.

problems.quote: The Right to Explanation clause in the 2023 Act
problems.problem: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 does not contain a Right to Explanation clause.
problems.correction: The 2023 Act does not provide a right to explanation
problems.verifierReason: DPDP Act 2023 lacks explicit right to explanation; correction accurately reflects this.

problems.quote: The Forest Rights Act, 2006, institutionalises a consent mechanism requiring free, prior, and informed consent of gram sabhas before diversion of forest land.
problems.problem: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 mandates consultation of gram sabhas, not free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC). FPIC for forest diversion is required under the Forest Conservation Rules and PESA, not the FRA.
problems.correction: The Forest Conservation Rules and PESA require free, prior, and informed consent of gram sabhas before diversion of forest land; the Forest Rights Act, 2006 mandates consultation.
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates FRA as requiring FPIC; correction accurately limits FPIC to rules/PESA and notes FRA only mandates consultation.

problems.quote: India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, requires data fiduciaries to provide accessible information about automated processing affecting data principals.
problems.problem: The DPDP Act, 2023 has general transparency obligations but no specific requirement for information about automated processing akin to GDPR Article 22.
problems.correction: India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, requires data fiduciaries to provide accessible information about processing activities affecting data principals.
problems.verifierReason: Original overstates DPDP Act's automated‑processing disclosure; correction correctly reflects general transparency obligations.

problems.quote: The All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968, categorise conflicts into (a) direct pecuniary interest in a contract or licence, (b) indirect interest through spouse or dependent relatives, and (c) pos
problems.problem: The All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968 do not formally categorise conflicts of interest into these three categories; they contain separate provisions on gifts, private trade, investments, and a cooling-off period for post-retirement employment.
problems.correction: The All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968 contain provisions on gifts, private trade, investments, and a cooling-off period for post-retirement employment, but do not formally categorise conflicts
problems.verifierReason: Original invents specific conflict categories not in the Rules; correction accurately describes the actual provisions.

problems.quote: The Indian judiciary operates under the Supreme Court’s administrative control (Article 146)
problems.problem: Article 146 concerns appointments of Supreme Court staff only; it does not give the Supreme Court administrative control over the entire Indian judiciary. High Courts control subordinate courts under Article 235.
problems.correction: The Indian judiciary operates with the Supreme Court at the apex; High Courts have administrative control over subordinate courts under Article 235, while the Supreme Court’s administrative control un
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates Article 146; correction accurately describes Supreme Court's limited administrative role and High Courts' control under Article 235.

problems.quote: “regulatory capture” arises when emotional regulation fails
problems.problem: The NGT’s 2021 order on the Char Dham highway project did not contain this statement; it is an invented quote attributing regulatory capture to emotional regulation failure.
problems.correction: The NGT’s 2021 order mandated a cumulative impact assessment but did not link regulatory capture to emotional regulation.
problems.verifierReason: Quote is fabricated; NGT order required cumulative impact assessment, not linking regulatory capture to emotional regulation.

problems.quote: The Supreme Court’s “Judicial Wellness Initiative” (2021) introduced mandatory quarterly self‑assessment using the Judicial Stress Inventory
problems.problem: No such mandatory quarterly self-assessment program was instituted by the Supreme Court in 2021; the described pilot data is not from an official source.
problems.correction: The Supreme Court has not instituted a mandatory quarterly Judicial Stress Inventory self-assessment; judicial wellness measures remain voluntary and decentralized.
problems.verifierReason: No mandatory quarterly Judicial Stress Inventory self-assessment exists; wellness measures are voluntary/decentralized.

problems.quote: Article 51A(g) (fundamental duty to protect natural resources)
problems.problem: Article 51A(g) of the Indian Constitution states the fundamental duty "to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life", not "natural resources".
problems.correction: Article 51A(g) (fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment)
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates Art 51A(g) duty; correction accurately cites "natural environment" per Constitution text.

problems.quote: The Disaster Management Act, 2005, provides that orders restricting fundamental rights must be necessary and proportionate, with periodic review mechanisms.
problems.problem: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 does not explicitly require that orders restricting fundamental rights be necessary and proportionate; that requirement arises from constitutional law (Articles 19, 21). The Act provides for review mechanisms but not the proportionality standard for fundamental righ
problems.correction: The Disaster Management Act, 2005, provides for periodic review mechanisms; necessity and proportionality of rights restrictions are constitutional requirements.
problems.verifierReason: DMA 2005 does not set proportionality standard for rights; that is constitutional; correction correctly separates.

problems.quote: In the Hasdeo Arand matter, the NGT halted a coal‑block allocation after the Gram Sabha’s opposition was overlooked
problems.problem: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) did not halt the coal-block allocation; it dismissed a petition challenging the environment clearance for the Parsa coal mine. The coal-block auctions were later cancelled by the Chhattisgarh government.
problems.correction: In the Hasdeo Arand matter, the Chhattisgarh government cancelled coal-block auctions after Gram Sabha opposition was overlooked
problems.verifierReason: NGT did not halt allocation; Chhattisgarh govt cancelled auctions; correction reflects actual events.

problems.quote: 2020 National Academies report Gene Drives on the Horizon
problems.problem: The National Academies report "Gene Drives on the Horizon" was published in 2016, not 2020.
problems.correction: 2016 National Academies report Gene Drives on the Horizon
problems.verifierReason: Report published 2016, not 2020; correction accurate.

problems.quote: Right to Explanation emerging under the EU GDPR Article 22
problems.problem: GDPR Article 22 addresses automated individual decision‑making; the "right to explanation" is not established in Article 22 but is discussed in Recital 71 and linked to Article 15 (right of access).
problems.correction: Right to Explanation discussed in GDPR Recital 71 and Article 15
problems.verifierReason: Right to explanation not in Art.22; Recital 71 & Art.15 cover it; correction correct.

problems.quote: 2010 Oxford Principles (Rayner et al.)
problems.problem: The Oxford Principles for geoengineering governance were published in 2009, not 2010.
problems.correction: 2009 Oxford Principles (Rayner et al.)
problems.verifierReason: Oxford Principles published 2009; correction fixes year.
